item.title: Geneva to Host FIDE World Championship Match 2026: D Gukesh vs. Javokhir Sindarov
item.description: The International Chess Federation (FIDE) has officially announced that Geneva, Switzerland, will host the FIDE World Championship Match 2026, scheduled from November 25 to December 15, 2026. World Champion D Gukesh of India will go against Challenger Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan for the biggest title in the game. With both grandmasters turning 20 years old by the start of the event, this match will mark the youngest World Championship contest in chess history. Graphic: FIDE

item.title: The rise of Kerala's young chess prodigy Aadik Theophane Lenin
item.description: At just 14, Aadik Theophane Lenin is one of India's fastest-rising chess talents. After earning his first International Master norm and gaining an incredible 264 Elo points in just two tournaments, he stands on the threshold of an extraordinary career. But behind every achievement lies years of sacrifice, unwavering family support, and a new challenge: the financial burden of pursuing the Grandmaster dream. This is the inspiring story of a gifted young player, the community rallying behind him, and why timely support could help shape India's next Grandmaster.

item.title: Behind the Lens: The Naroditsky Memorial Rapid and Blitz
item.description: The inaugural Naroditsky Memorial Rapid & Blitz in Charlotte was more than a chess tournament; it was a celebration of GM Daniel Naroditsky's legacy! Through the lens of Charlotte Chess Center photographer Kelly Centrelli, the event comes alive in a collection of memorable images and the stories behind them. Read on to see the tournament through the eyes of the person who captured it all. Photos: Kelly Centrelli.

item.title: Apoorv Kamble Dominates at 2nd ChessFusion Rapid Rating 2026
item.description: IM Apoorv Kamble scored an unbeaten 8.5/9 to win All India Fide Rated Rapid 2026 powered by Chessfusion. In the final round, Apoorv defeated the tournament leader, Anuj Shrivatri, to clinch the title. 10 players scored 8/9 points to secure 2nd to 11th positions, respectively, on tiebreak scores; Bhuvan Krishna Prasanth and Anuj Shrivatri secured podium finishes. The tournament was held at Smriti Academy, Bangalore, on 11th July 2026. Photos: Lavanya K/Chessfusion

item.title: When Chess Met Robotics: Inside IIT Delhi's RoboGambit
item.description: We’re used to seeing AI crush grandmasters in a blink. But what happens when you take that brilliant silicon brain and force it to grapple with the physical world? At IIT Delhi’sRoboGambit, we didn't just see perfect chess engines; we watched them sweat. Or rather, we watched their robotic arms fumble, stutter, and run out of time while trying to move a simple plastic piece. It’s a humble, slightly chaotic reminder that while thinking about chess is easy, actually playing it with grace, speed, and under pressure is a whole different beast.

item.title: Government of India & AICF Launch ‘CHESS+’ to Bring Structured Chess Education into Schools
item.description: In a major step toward developing a grass-roots chess culture in India, Union Minister Shri Jayant Chaudhary has officially launched CHESS+. The nationwide initiative is designed to introduce a structured chess curriculum into school education, bringing expert coaching, competition, and mentorship directly to classrooms. The initiative is being implemented jointly by the All India Chess Federation and the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.

item.title: Vignesh N R, A Qil A Lauddin, and Thejkumar Triumph at the 2nd DAV–Go Checkmate International Chess Prix 2026
item.description: The 2nd DAV–Go Checkmate International Chess Prix 2026 concluded after six action-packed days of elite competition. Organized by Go Checkmate Pte Ltd from June 22 to 27, 2026, the festival gathered 352 players across various categories, including Grandmasters, International Masters, and ambitious juniors from over 11 countries. Vignesh NR won the Gm/IM Round Robin with 6/9 points. Photos: Vidhyavarshni/ Go Checkmate Pte Ltd

item.title: 2nd Siliguri FIDE Rated Classical Tournament 2026 to Take Place from 11th to 16th August
item.description: The Siliguri Chess Guardian’s Club (SCGC) is set to host the 2nd Siliguri International FIDE Rated Classical Chess Tournament 2026 from 11th August to 16th August 2026 at the air-conditioned Shilpanchal Bhawan, Burdwan Road, Siliguri, West Bengal. Building on the success of its inaugural 2025 edition, SCGC is organizing this year's event on an even grander scale, inviting several Grandmasters and International Masters to compete. Register Fast!!

item.title: ChessBase India hits 3 million subscribers on YouTube
item.description: On 26th of July 2026, ChessBase India hit 3 million subscribers on their YouTube channel. In this article we tell you the stories of this channel through numbers! The channel is now 11 years old and has 19246 videos! A lot of people have contributed towards its success. After Gotham Chess, Hikaru Nakamura, ChessBase India becomes the third chess channel to hit 3 million subscribers.

item.title: New Champions Crowned at the 2026 U.S. National Championships in Saint Louis
item.description: America’s premier chess hub witnessed a spectacular showcase of talent as the 2026 U.S. Junior, U.S. Junior Girls', U.S. Senior, and the inaugural Saint Louis edition of the U.S. Senior Women’s National Championships concluded at the Saint Louis Chess Club. Held from July 13–24, 2026, the invitation-only event brought together top-tier prodigies and esteemed veterans vying for four national crowns and a total prize pool of $285,000. Photo: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Chess Super GM Anish Giri Joins BASILISK, Science's Esports Team
item.description: The world of chess has another blockbuster move. World No. 8 Anish Giri has joined BASILISK, where he will team up with Vincent Keymer to form one of the strongest duos in competitive chess. Giri is expected to make his first appearance for the organization at the upcoming Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz.

item.title: Mentors Needed: Help Checkmate Betul Bring Chess to Girls Across India
item.description: Checkmate Betul is expanding, and mentors are needed!What started as a small local initiative has grown into a movement empowering girls across India through chess. Got1 hour a weekto help a young player find her footing? A few years ago, Checkmate Betul was a small idea with a simple goal: get more girls in Betul in front of a chessboard. It has not stayed small. What began as a handful of local lessons has turned into a network of online classes reaching girls across Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, and now Nagaland, a state where opportunities for girls to learn and compete in chess have historically been hard to come by. That kind of growth is worth celebrating on its own. (Photos: Checkmate Betul)

item.title: Tharun Pranav G. B. Wins RV Chess Academy 2nd Below-1800 Classical Rating 2026
item.description: Tharun Pranav G B scored 8/9 points to win the RV Chess Academy 2nd International FIDE Rating Chess Tournament for Below 1800. 6 players scored 7.5/9 points to finish in 2nd to 7th places according to tiebreak scores. Sriman V and Pradheep B secured 2nd and 3rd places. The tournament was organised by RV Chess Academy at New Prince Shri Bhavani College of Engineering, Chennai. The total prize fund was ₹4,00,000, with top 3 prizes of ₹40,000, ₹30,000 and ₹20,000, along with trophies. Photos: RV Chess Academy

item.title: Aswath S Wins Serbia Open 2026 Just After Becoming India's 98th Grandmaster
item.description: Aswath S scored an unbeaten 7.5/9 points in a super-strong field to win the Serbia Open 2026 (Masters). Aswath made his final GM Norm in the Pune Round Robin event, where he won the last game on demand. Here in Serbia, Aswath defeated GM Mitrabha Guha in an important clash of the penultimate round. He gained a half-point lead going into the final round and drew against Ethan Vaz, who also recently became India's 96th Grandmaster. Matfey Yurasov and Ethan Vaz finished in 2nd and 3rd places, respectively. Photos: Serbia Chess Federation

item.title: Viswanathan Anand Takes Charge as FIDE Interim President
item.description: In a major development in the governance of world chess, FIDE President Arkady Dvorkovich has announced that he is voluntarily suspending his powers and duties as President with immediate effect. In accordance with FIDE, Viswanathan Anand, the 15th World Chess Champion and current Deputy President of FIDE, has taken over as the Interim President of the International Chess Federation.
